quantity: Active-standby leakage at 25 C, nominal voltage, macro incl. periphery (mW per decimal MB)
value: LOW 0.21 (R01, 3 nm, 1-CLM); PLANNING 0.33 (geometric mean of R01 and R02); HIGH 0.52 (R02, 7 nm UHD). EXP-0008 used 0.60 flat for its 'hot nominal' planning; it is reproduced as a separate input, not as this model's planning value.

value: ASAP7 6T cell SPICE (R13): at 0.70 V the hold leakage rises 1.6x (50 C), 3.4x (75 C), 4.9x (85 C), 10.2x (105 C) relative to 25 C; at 0.35 V it rises 3.1x / 9.6x / 14.9x / 34x. Old-node measured retention modes (R05 1.46x, R06 1.50x per 10 C) agree with the low-voltage curve. quantity: Periphery share of macro standby leakage
value: 0.30 (R01: bitline prechargers alone are 10%; decoders, sense amplifiers, drivers and clocking assumed to bring the periphery to ~30%). Range 0.15-0.45.
label: ASSUMPTION

quantity: Retention modes and their leakage ratio to active standby at the same temperature
value: LIGHT_SLEEP (BL precharge off, array nominal, periphery on): 0.90 (R01 T1). DEEP_SLEEP_NOMINAL (periphery off, array at nominal V): 1 - B3 = 0.70 (ASSUMPTION; upper end of R04). RETENTION_VRET (periphery off, array at V_ret): (1 - B3) x array power ratio from R13, which is temperature dependent: at 0.35 V 0.108 (25 C), 0.33 (85 C) -> 0.076 / 0.23 total; at 0.45 V 0.22 / 0.47 -> 0.15 / 0.33 total. R03 (7 nm PDK, 0.25) sits between. OPTIMISTIC_BODY_BIAS: 0.013 (R05 T1, FD-SOI with reverse body bias; not available in FinFET) kept as a bound only. SHUTDOWN (0.002, R03) loses data and is never used as retention.
label: T2 modeled ratios anchored by T1 (R01, R05) and T2 (R03)

value: PLANNING 0.35 V (ASAP7 hold state converges and keeps hold SNM > 0 at 0.35 V across 25-105 C per hold_snm table; no verified modern-node DRV figure found, R18 excluded); sweep 0.25-0.50 V. Retention at 0.25 V is marginal at 105 C (q-low node rises above 0.2 V in SPICE).

value: per-macro wake t_macro: LOW 10 ns (R03 10 cycles at ~1 GHz), PLANNING 200 ns (R05, 128 KiB-class macro with in-rush limiting), HIGH 1 us (ASSUMPTION for a 256 KB macro at a tighter in-rush limit); macros per domain wake in groups of LOW 64 / PLANNING 8 / HIGH 1 (in-rush limit, ASSUMPTION); floor 2 ns (R01 one cycle). Light sleep exits in one cycle (R01).
label: ASSUMPTION ranges anchored on R05 (T1, 22 nm) and R03 (T2)

quantity: Wake energy per MB of domain
value: array rail capacitance ~4 nF per MB (8e6 cells x ~0.5 fF per cell to the cell rail: single-fin PU source/junction and PU gate at EOT 1 nm; KNOWN physics, order-of-magnitude); full array-rail swing 0.35 -> 0.75 V draws E = C x Vdd x dV = 1.2 uJ/MB (HIGH, applies to RETENTION_VRET exit); periphery-only restore (DEEP_SLEEP_NOMINAL exit) ~12% of that = 0.15 uJ/MB (PLANNING); LOW 0.02 uJ/MB (R03-class, 4 KB segments at 41-cycle break-even). Sequencer 10 pJ per macro. Sleep entry: 0 (stored rail energy dissipates). No measured modern-node macro wake energy exists.
label: ASSUMPTION (physics-based estimate, R11 method)

value: one power switch set per macro (256 KB, EXP-0008 A9) is supported by every compiler source (R04 per instance; R03 per 4 KB segment; R05 per 4 KiB macro with 2.1% area); layer domains are groups of macros switched together; the model sweeps domain = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 layers / whole model. Independent array-voltage regulation per macro is NOT assumed: V_ret is a shared retention rail per domain.
label: T1/T2/T3 supported at macro granularity; domain grouping ASSUMPTION

value: layer execution time in burst mode = layer bytes / engine bandwidth with engine bandwidth 8 TB/s (EXP-0006 tile aggregate, TARGET) and 1 TB/s sensitivity; in paced mode the token period is spread evenly over the L layers (layer time = 1 / (R x L)). No physical clock is claimed; EXP-0005 RTL is cycle-exact but unclocked.
label: TARGET / ASSUMPTION

value: unchanged from EXP-0008 (A6/A7/A13): 4.0 pJ/bit planning path; channel-busy fraction at IDD2N, rest IDD2P (5.4 mW); between sessions self-refresh (0.77 mW at 25 C, 9.8 mW at 85 C, log-interpolated) when the idle gap is >= 1 s, power-down otherwise; in the duty-cycle sweep the idle fraction is charged the cheaper of power-down and self-refresh at the idle temperature.

value: NOT a retention mode (data lost). Between sessions the array is powered off (residual switch leakage 0.002 x active, R03) and the weights are reloaded from external storage at the next session: E_reload = EXP-0008 cold-start energy (weights x 8 x (4.0 pJ/bit LPDDR + 0.09 pJ/bit x 1.65 SRAM write)) = 13.2 mJ for Falcon-E 1B; first-token latency = reload time at 1-4 GB/s (0.1-0.4 s). Priced as a comparison row so retention is judged against the obvious alternative.

value: JEDEC/Micron IDD values are specified at the maximum operating case temperature, so the IDD2N (32.1 mW) and IDD2P (5.4 mW) charged during generation are hot-corner maxima at every temperature while the SRAM side uses 25 C measurements at 25 C. This favours residency at 25 C by up to ~27 mW of the 345 mW LPDDR total (Falcon-E 1B at 25 tok/s). Planning is left as EXP-0008 defined it; a sensitivity row halves IDD2N/IDD2P at 25 C.
